newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares regret early gains, slip 0.41pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares regret early gains, slip 0.41pct.

text.p: Greek shares were weak in active late trade and failed to hold on to early gains on optimism over the outcome of OTE telecom's part-flotation which ends June 13.
Shares of OTE fell 3.36 percent, surrendering all of Wednesday's gains in active trading and brokers said an arbitrage-like behaviour by institutional players accounted for the selling pressure.
"There was a reversal of yesterday's picture, with foreign and domestic portfolios taking profits against a substantially lower price arrived at in the book-building process," said a broker.
The institutional book-building in OTE shares is carried out at 6,200-6,900 drachmas per share with retail investors subscribing to the public offering at 6,000-6,700 drachmas per share.
The Greek State, currently owner of 92.43 percent of OTE's stock, offers a total of 45 million shares -- 10.7 percent.
Another 2.1 million shares will probably be offered by the state due to increased demand and global co-ordinators are preparing to allocate an extra 6.33 million shares, brokers said.
And on Thursday, CSFB started coverage of OTE with a 'hold' recommendation, on a positive outlook for pricing and volume growth contributing to sustained, above-average cash flow and earnings growth.
But it noted that the sharp appreciation rendered the stock one of the most expensive telecoms in Europe and saw limited upside potential from current price levels.
"OTE's stock is cheap-to-fairly valued and has good prospects," said Stathis Nazos, fund manager at ABN-AMRO mutual funds.
In the long-term, it will be one of the bourse's best performing stocks, he added.
OTE's issue was expected to have a positive long-term effect on Greek equities.

"The large size of the flotation will temper the stock's volatility as the free float increases," said Nazos. "But it will provide the bourse with greater exposure to global funds which in the long run will be favourable."
The broader market would stay in a trading range.
"The market has had good performance this year and should now assimillate its gains," Nazos said.
It is in a trading range with limited downside risk and upside scope extending to the recently recorded highs in the 1,750-point region, he added.
"We will see the market climbing to 2,000 by year-end as long as the macroeconomic environment and political stability remain intact," Nazos forecast.
The Athens general index drifted 0.41 percent or 6.66 points lower from Wednesday's 1,638.56 close, settling at 1,631.90.
Banks slipped 0.27 percent. Industrials were flat and construction was active, rising 2.99 percent helped by select large-cap shares.
Turnover rose to 30 billion drachmas on volume of 6.0 million shares with OTE, large banks, cement and high-tech stocks contributing most of the activity.
Advancers led decliners 116 to 105 with 23 shares unchanged on 244 traded.
